A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same lmKAN research and contain readable main text, figures, algorithms, equations, and Appendices A–F. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original function-approximation, methane, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, FastKAN-comparison, and GPU-timing results, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The multivariate spline lookup layers, static percentile grids, Hessian regularization, preconditioning alternatives, and multistage training remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices B–E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic 32-to-1 and 32-to-32 approximation tasks, four methane representations, CIFAR-10, and downsampled ImageNet. The added methane-source citation does not introduce another dataset.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MLPs, linear-layer timing baselines, and FastKAN remain in their corresponding comparisons, including reduced-training-budget MLP controls. Newly cited KAN approaches are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The splits, architectures, training budgets, augmentations, and metrics are retained. Examples include the methane 7,000,000/300,000/432,488 split and 81-by-81 ImageNet inputs. Section 4's new summary about matching backbones describes the existing design.

E4.justification: The grid-resolution and Hessian-regularization ablations, preconditioning comparisons, training illustrations, and CUDA scaling analyses are retained. Figures 7, 14–19, and 21–24 provide the same analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix F.1 retains 10 warm-up runs and 20 timed runs. Neither version adds training-seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The 6.0× and 4.2× synthetic-task FLOP reductions are retained; v2's explicit reference to roughly one thousand-fold methane savings restates the 1021.5× value already displayed in v1 Figure 9.

T1.justification: The representation formulas, computational-cost reasoning, Hessian finite differences, and methane invariant polynomials are retained. The standard KAN-layer equation becomes inline, shifting subsequent equation numbers without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central drop-in-replacement and efficiency claims retain their meaning and scope, including the abstract and conclusion's quantitative claims. The introduction highlights FastKAN accuracy and training stability already discussed in v1 Section 4.4 and reorganizes the existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly explains that experimental diversity was prioritized over very large scale or architectural complexity. Appendix E.2 removes the qualification that experiments favoring gamma = 0.3 were non-systematic. The main mechanism explanations and Section 5 limitations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 replaces the commit-pinned FastKAN training-script link with a master-branch link, removing exact source-version information. The implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and benchmarking disclosures otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on KAN transformers, quantum architecture search, PointNet, two piecewise-linear KAN approaches, and the methane dataset's source. Section 2 also narrows the characterization of KAN shortcomings and removes a criticism of UKAN's comparisons, modestly broadening and balancing the positioning.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the contribution bullets, edits portions of the related-work and experiment introductions, removes an illustrative grid-occupancy example, and corrects wording throughout the appendices. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 5, 7, and 10 move to earlier pages, with accompanying text reflow, spacing, and caption edits. The first-page preprint footer is removed. The figures, table, and algorithms retain their substantive display content.

improvement.justification: The expanded discussion of prior KAN and piecewise-linear approaches, explicit methane-source attribution, and clearer prose modestly improve context and readability while preserving the scientific evidence. These benefits are tempered by the loss of a commit-specific FastKAN reference and the removed non-systematic-experiment caveat in Appendix E.2.
